clue.text: In Coleraine dancing marks observance of formality

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the answer is also a noun meaning a set of rites

indicators.note: In at the head says the next piece, marks, goes inside the shuffled town name
dancing letters move about, so the town name Coleraine is rearranged

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish town's dances are a formal ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges COLERAINE (a town in Northern Ireland) and 'In' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial is a prescribed system of rites, the formal side of an occasion.

clue.text: Boy in famine abandoning Southern State capital

indicators.note: in puts the boy inside the shortened famine word
abandoning says the southern letter is dropped

parts.note: a famine is a scarcity of food
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A boy in a southern famine leaves his state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops the S from the famine word, leaving CARCITY, and 'in' puts the boy inside. 'Southern State' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'State capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carson City is the capital of the US state of Nevada.

clue.text: Underwater valley a strain to climb

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a strain is a tune, an air

explanation.surface: Climbing out of a sunken valley is a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like effort, but it is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: A ria is a drowned river valley flooded by the sea.

clue.text: Corny stuff recited in difficult passages?

indicators.note: recited means spoken, so a word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a maze is a confusing network of passages

explanation.surface: Trite phrases repeated in hard bits of text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests trite but means made of corn; 'passages' are paths, not text.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is corn, the cereal crop, so it is literally corny material.

clue.text: Short prison "vacation" after arrest of a man

indicators.note: after says the holiday word comes after the prison word
short says the prison word loses its last letter

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison

indicators.note: arrest of says the holiday word holds the a inside

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays

explanation.surface: A brief jail stint is no holiday after a man is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK, British slang for jail, loses its K; HOLS is British for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas is a man's first name, so it is an example of a man.

clue.text: Fleet Street keeping mum in articles

indicators.note: in says the street with its mum goes inside the two articles

parts.note: a and a are indefinite articles

indicators.note: keeping says the street holds the mother inside

parts.note: RD, for road, here stands as a street abbreviation
ma is another word for mum

explanation.surface: London's newspaper district keeps quiet in its pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet Street' reads as London's newspaper district; it splits into the definition and RD. 'mum' looks like silent but is mother.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships.

clue.text: Engineer pardon for member of audience

indicators.note: a member of an audience hears rather than reads, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: 'Pardon?' and 'What?' are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: An engineer begs a spectator's forgiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pardon' is not forgiveness but the request to repeat, 'What?', which said aloud is the engineer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: James Watt was the Scottish engineer who improved the steam engine.

clue.text: One's soft, yet as an alternative it hurts!

indicators.note: an alternative is another arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: 'Ouch!' is what you say when it hurts

explanation.surface: Someone tender-hearted, yet another way of feeling pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alternative' rearranges YET AS AN; then OUCH. 'One's soft' means someone who is soft, an easy mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy touch is a person readily persuaded to give money, a soft target.

clue.text: Tip it down side of the mouth

indicators.note: of the mouth means spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Spit out of one side of your mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip it down' is British for raining heavily. 'side of the mouth' looks like anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: To pour with rain is to rain in torrents, which is what tipping it down means.

clue.text: Maiden in Coleraine wildly spending money

indicators.note: in places the maiden's letter inside the scrambled town
wildly says the letters of Coleraine are thrown into a new order

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman in a Northern Irish town goes on a spending spree.
explanation.walkthrough: COLERAINE again, a town in Northern Ireland, rearranged by 'wildly' with M put 'in'. 'spending money' is what you actually have to spend.
explanation.definitionFit: Real income is earnings adjusted for inflation, the purchasing power left to spend.

clue.text: Best of the Beatles in time covered by Slash

indicators.note: covered by says the time letter sits inside the word for slash

parts.note: slash is British slang for urinating, as is pee

explanation.surface: Guitarist Slash outshines the Beatles' finest for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: Pete Best was the Beatles' drummer before Ringo; 'Slash' looks like the guitarist but is British slang for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Pete Best drummed for the Beatles in their early years, so the Best of that band is him.

clue.text: Day to appreciate rising chill

parts.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: to dig something is to appreciate it

explanation.surface: A day for enjoying a rising chill in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the appreciation word upwards, as befits a down clue; 'chill' looks like a noun but stands as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigid means very cold, so it can stand for chill used as an adjective.

clue.text: Circle, gaining speed, US airport

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
to hare is to run at speed

explanation.surface: A traffic circle picks up pace near an American airport.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Hare is Chicago's main international airport.

clue.text: A fan of lean cuisine, I love eating junk etc that could make me look stocky?

definitions.text: that could make me look stocky?

indicators.note: eating says the fan of lean food takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: Jack Sprat of the nursery rhyme could eat no fat

indicators.note: to junk is to throw out, so the letters of etc are scrambled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A slimmer who loves junk food worries about looking stocky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'junk' shuffles the 'etc' letters and 'eating' puts them inside the nursery-rhyme figure Jack Sprat, who would eat no fat. The definition: a wrong frame shape squashes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Altering a picture's width-to-height proportion can squash it so that figures look squat.

clue.text: Outdated language of ex-Murdoch hack's leader

parts.note: outdated things are old
the late novelist Iris Murdoch, a Murdoch no longer living

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of hack's

explanation.surface: A former Murdoch journalist's chief speaks in an obsolete tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murdoch' suggests the press baron and his hacks; it is the novelist Iris Murdoch, and 'ex-' marks her as late.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Irish is the earliest written form of the Gaelic language of Ireland.

clue.text: Old copy of Lancet, perhaps, describing epidural?

explanation.surface: An old medical journal describes a spinal anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lancet is a medical journal; the second reading has 'number' as a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdated issue of a periodical is a past one; and an epidural deadens sensation in the lower spine.

clue.text: Deciding tie might be fun with a clip

indicators.note: might be says the letters could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A clip-on accessory could make a necktie more fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' asks for an anagram of FUN and A CLIP; 'tie' is a sporting fixture, not neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The cup final is the match that decides who wins a knockout competition.

clue.text: Club concerned with this type of transfer?

parts.note: an iron is a golf club
on means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: A golf club is concerned with a player's transfer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' and 'transfer' suggest football; the club is a golf iron, and the transfer a picture applied with heat.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron-on transfer is a design fixed to fabric by pressing with a hot iron.

clue.text: Kirk got lambasted for restricting assembly of elders

indicators.note: restricting says the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A church elder is criticised for hemming in a council.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'KirK GOT LAmbasted'. A kgotla is a tribal assembly in Botswana.
explanation.definitionFit: A kgotla is a public meeting of village elders in Botswana, a traditional court.

clue.text: State, strangely, wants to be constricted?

indicators.note: to be with constricted says the scrambled letters end up held inside the snake

parts.note: a boa is the snake that constricts its prey

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of wants are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A state oddly desires to be restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' makes TSWAN of the wanting word; 'to be constricted' puts it inside the constrictor snake, as if squeezed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Botswana is a country in southern Africa.

clue.text: Young Conservatives split over name for their possible sponsor?

indicators.note: split says the word for over is cut open by the youth group's letters

parts.note: too means over, excessively
YC stands for Young Conservatives, the Tory youth wing

explanation.surface: The youth wing of the Tories divides over the name of a financial backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split over' reads as a party quarrel; 'over' means excessively, as in too much, and 'split' says that word is broken open.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy magnate is just the sort of rich donor a youth party might court.

clue.text: All the best syrup left in dip

parts.note: syrup is sticky stuff, goo

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside the word for dip

parts.note: to duck is to dip down

explanation.surface: Best syrup is set aside for a dunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell wish for success, much as 'all the best' is said on parting.

clue.text: Material cracking and rolling (not hard)

parts.note: cracking means excellent, fab

indicators.note: not says the hard letter is removed

parts.note: rolling in it means rich
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Cloth that is splitting and rolling, but not stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' and 'rolling' look like actions on cloth; both are adjectives, excellent and wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric is a woven or knitted cloth.

clue.text: Birds on rails initially nearly closed networks

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the words on and rails

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed or nearly so
LANs are local area networks of computers

explanation.surface: Model trains on rails run on a nearly finished closed system.
explanation.walkthrough: TO is the adverb in 'pull the door to'. LANS are computer local area networks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ortolans are small buntings, once eaten as a delicacy in France.

clue.text: Statesman rebuffed in favour henceforth

indicators.note: rebuffed says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political leader is rejected in a plea for future goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: The run 'favoUR HENceforth' is turned round by 'rebuffed'; 'in' says it lies within those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a leading statesman.

clue.text: Crystal not a thing that's firm on the inside

indicators.note: on the inside places the firm's letters within the word for nothing

parts.note: nil means nothing, not a thing
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A crystal is nothing solid inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective but is a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nicol is a calcite prism used to polarise light, made from a crystal.

clue.text: Screen means Sky can be shown regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Sky TV can be shown on a regular screen.
explanation.walkthrough: Every other letter of 'MeAnS SkY' gives the answer; 'Sky' suggests the broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask is to screen something from view.

clue.text: Do without piano, aspiring to culture?

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the word for do

parts.note: a do is a party
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A party with no piano music wants to seem cultured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a noun, a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone with pretensions to artistic taste.

clue.text: Tiny amount of comfort food?

parts.note: a crumb of comfort is a tiny amount of solace; read literally the crumb is of the staple food

explanation.surface: Barely any reassurance on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a crumb of comfort' is read with the comfort as a food.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumb is a minute fragment, and one from a loaf is the smallest bit of a staple food.

clue.text: Remains holder after elimination of sides from tournament

indicators.note: removing the outer parts of tournament leaves a stretch from inside it

explanation.surface: A trophy is held after teams are knocked out of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' look like teams knocked out; trim the outside of 'tOURNament'.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn holds a person's ashes after cremation.

clue.text: Strike back in tie

indicators.note: back says the word for strike is read in reverse

parts.note: tonk is slang for hitting hard

explanation.surface: Hitting back in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: TONK, turned round by 'back', is British slang for a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To knot is to tie, and a knot is a tie in a rope.

clue.text: Original Coleraine artisan finally displaying great craft

indicators.note: original suggests something newly made, so the letters are reworked
finally takes the last letter of artisan

explanation.surface: An inventive craftsman from a Northern Irish town shows off fine work.
explanation.walkthrough: COLERAINE, a Northern Irish town, plus N (end of 'artisan') are rearranged by 'Original'. 'craft' is a vessel, not a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean liner is a large passenger ship, a big seagoing vessel.
